steps.step: Soak the potato wedges in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes to rinse away surface starch — this is what lets them crisp in the air fryer instead of turning soft.
Drain and pat the wedges completely dry with a clean towel — any leftover water turns to steam and stops browning.
Toss the wedges with olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for 3 minutes.
Arrange half the wedges in a single layer in the basket, skin-side down — crowding is the enemy of crisp edges here.
Air fry the first batch until deeply golden and crisp, shaking the basket halfway, about 16 to 18 minutes.
Repeat with the second batch of wedges, shaking halfway, until just as golden and crisp.
Combine both batches, sprinkle with parsley, and serve hot.
Pat the chicken breasts dry and rub both sides with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Meanwhile, warm the salsa in a small saucepan over medium heat until simmering, about 5 minutes — this stands in for the sauce a slow cooker would build on its own.
Grill the chicken with the lid down until deep grill marks form and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 6 minutes per side.
Move the chicken to a cutting board and rest 5 minutes so the juices settle back in.
Slice or shred the chicken, then spoon the warm salsa over the top and squeeze in the lime juice.
Serve warm in tortillas, over rice, or piled onto nachos.
Place the chicken breasts in the pressure cooker in a single layer.
Pour the salsa over the chicken, then sprinkle on the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes — plenty of time for the chicken to turn fork-tender without drying out.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release any that's left — natural release keeps the chicken from seizing up.
Shred the chicken right in the pot, stir it through the sauce, and squeeze in the lime juice. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve warm in tortillas, over rice, or piled onto nachos.
Pat the chicken breasts dry and season with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt on both sides.
Spread half the salsa over the bottom of a large skillet and set the chicken on top in a single layer.
Pour the remaining salsa over the chicken, cover, and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, covered, flipping once, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily, about 18 to 20 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate, shred with two forks, then stir it back into the skillet sauce with the lime juice. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve warm in tortillas, over rice, or piled onto nachos.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and brown the ground beef with the onion and garlic until the meat is no longer pink, about 8 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, kidney beans, chili powder, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes — just enough to marry the flavors since the beef and beans are already cooked.
Quick-release the pressure once the timer ends.
Switch back to sauté and simmer uncovered a few minutes until the chili reaches the thickness you like.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Ladle into bowls and top as you like.
In a bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
Add the frozen meatballs to the pressure cooker and pour the sauce over the top without stirring — a little sauce touching the bottom helps the pot come to pressure.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 5 minutes — frozen meatballs only need enough time to heat through and soak up the sauce.
Quick-release the pressure.
Switch to sauté and simmer uncovered, stirring gently, until the sauce thickens to a glossy glaze, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir once more, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve over rice or with toothpicks.
In a large skillet over medium heat, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic, and ginger until smooth and starting to bubble.
Add the frozen meatballs and stir to coat them in the sauce.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the meatballs are heated through, about 12 to 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer a few minutes more until the sauce clings to the meatballs in a glossy coat.
Stir once more, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve over rice or with toothpicks.
Add the dried lentils, carrot, onion, celery, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, garlic, thyme, salt, and black pepper to the pressure cooker.
Stir to combine, seal the lid, and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes — lentils go from raw to tender fast under pressure, no all-day simmer needed.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release any that's left.
Stir in the spinach and let it wilt in the residual heat with the lid ajar, about 2 minutes.
Taste for salt and pepper, then ladle into bowls.
Combine the dried lentils, carrot, onion, celery, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, garlic, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cover partway.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Taste for salt and pepper, then ladle into bowls.
Pat the ribs dry. Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then rub all over the ribs.
Set the ribs in the pressure cooker on the trivet, curling them to fit, and pour the apple cider vinegar and a splash of water into the bottom — the liquid is what lets the pot build steam.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 25 minutes — ribs turn fall-off-the-bone tender in a fraction of the slow cooker's time.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release the rest.
Carefully lift the ribs onto a foil-lined baking sheet and brush with half the BBQ sauce.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce bubbles and starts to caramelize, then brush with the remaining BBQ sauce.
Rest a few minutes, then cut into portions and serve with extra napkins.
Preheat the oven to 300°F and pat the ribs dry.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then rub all over the ribs.
Wrap the ribs tightly in foil with the apple cider vinegar drizzled inside — the sealed foil traps steam so the ribs braise in their own liquid, much like a slow cooker does.
Bake until the meat has pulled back from the bone ends and is fork-tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Carefully open the foil, watching for steam, brush the ribs with half the BBQ sauce, and raise the oven to 425°F.
Bake uncovered until the sauce sets and starts to caramelize at the edges, about 12 to 15 minutes.
Brush with the remaining BBQ sauce, rest a few minutes, then cut into portions.
Serve with extra napkins — these are messy in the best way.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and rub all over with the taco seasoning.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Meanwhile, simmer the onion, green chiles, and chicken broth in a small saucepan over medium heat until the onion softens, about 6 minutes.
Grill the chicken thighs, lid down, until charred and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 5 to 6 minutes per side.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice or shred it.
Toss the chicken with the warm onion-chile broth, then stir in the lime juice and cilantro.
Spoon into warm tortillas or bowls and load up your favorite toppings.
Scatter the onion in the bottom of the pressure cooker and set the chicken thighs on top.
Sprinkle the taco seasoning over the chicken, then add the green chiles and chicken broth.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes — thighs turn shreddy-tender fast under pressure.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release the rest.
Shred the chicken right in the pot, stir through the juices, then mix in the lime juice and cilantro.
Spoon into warm tortillas or bowls and load up your favorite toppings.
Heat the chicken broth in a large skillet over medium heat, add the onion, and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Nestle the chicken thighs into the skillet, sprinkle the taco seasoning over the top, and add the green chiles.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat, flipping once, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily, about 20 to 22 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and shred with two forks, then stir it back into the skillet with the pan juices.
Mix in the lime juice and cilantro.
Spoon into warm tortillas or bowls and load up your favorite toppings.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pat the salmon fillets dry, brush with olive oil, and season with garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Place the salmon skin-side down on the baking sheet. Squeeze lemon juice over the top and lay a lemon slice on each fillet.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and looks opaque in the center, about 12 to 14 minutes — a few minutes longer than the air fryer since the oven heats more gently around the fish.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour mixed with half the salt; beaten eggs; and breadcrumbs mixed with paprika, garlic powder, and remaining salt.
Dredge each chicken tender in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumb mix until coated.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and set a wire rack inside a baking sheet — the rack lets air move underneath so the bottom crisps instead of steaming.
Arrange the tenders on the rack in a single layer and mist both sides with cooking spray.
Bake until deep golden and the thickest piece reaches 165°F, about 18 to 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Rest 2 minutes so the crust stays crisp, then serve with your favorite dip.
Pat the firm tofu cubes very dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, toss the tofu with soy sauce, maple syrup, sesame oil, and garlic powder. Sprinkle on cornstarch and toss until every cube looks dusty and coated.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread the tofu in a single layer with space between the pieces — crowding traps steam and keeps the oven from browning it the way the air fryer's tight airflow does.
Bake until deeply golden and crisp on the edges, flipping once halfway, about 28 to 30 minutes.
Top with scallions and serve over rice or in a grain bowl.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Pat the shrimp dry and toss with melted butter, garlic, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the shrimp in a single layer in a baking dish.
Bake until pink, curled, and opaque all the way through, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Toss with lemon juice and parsley right in the dish, then serve straight from the oven over pasta, rice, or salad.
Pat the shrimp dry and toss with melted butter, garlic, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Preheat the broiler and set an oven rack about 6 inches from the heat.
Spread the shrimp in a single layer on a sheet pan, leaving space between each piece so they char instead of steam.
Broil until pink, curled, and lightly charred at the edges, about 4 to 5 minutes — watch closely, broilers work fast.
Toss with lemon juice and parsley right on the pan. Serve right away over pasta, rice, or salad.
Add the dried black beans, onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir well.
Cover and cook on low until the beans are fully tender and starting to fall apart, about 8 hours — no overnight soak needed, the slow cooker just takes its place.
Mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt. Serve hot.
Add the dried black beans, onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and salt to a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer and cover partway.
Simmer, stirring occasionally and adding a splash more broth if it thickens too fast, until the beans are fully tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours — unsoaked beans just need the extra time on the stove.
Mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt. Serve hot.
Place the chicken breasts in the slow cooker.
Add the chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and half the BBQ sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken shreds easily with two forks, about 5 hours (or 3 hours on high).
Transfer the chicken to a board and shred with two forks — it should pull apart with almost no resistance.
Return the chicken to the pot, stir in the remaining BBQ sauce, and let it sit uncovered a few minutes to soak in.
Serve on buns or over rice.
Place the chicken breasts in a large skillet.
Add the chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and half the BBQ sauce.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over medium-low heat, flipping once, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily, about 22 to 25 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a board and shred with two forks.
Return the chicken to the skillet, stir in the remaining BBQ sauce, and simmer uncovered 2 minutes until glossy.
Serve on buns or over rice.
In a skillet on the stovetop, cook the bacon until crisp, about 6 minutes. Scoop out most of it and set aside, leaving a little fat behind — a slow cooker can't crisp bacon on its own.
Add the onion and garlic to the same skillet and cook until soft, about 3 minutes.
Transfer the bacon fat, onion, and garlic to the slow cooker along with the russet potatoes, chicken broth, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 6 hours (or 3 hours on high).
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot until the soup looks thick but still chunky.
Stir in the milk, sour cream, and cheddar cheese until melted and creamy. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved bacon and scallions.
In a large pot, cook the bacon until crisp, about 6 minutes. Scoop out most of it and set aside, leaving a little fat in the pot.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the russet potatoes, chicken broth, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer, partially covered, until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 18 to 20 minutes.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot until the soup looks thick but still chunky.
Stir in the milk, sour cream, and cheddar cheese until melted and creamy. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with reserved bacon and scallions.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the italian sausage links on all sides until browned, about 5 minutes — this is the flavor step a slow cooker can't do on its own.
Toss the bell peppers and onion with the garlic powder, italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper, then spread them in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Nestle the browned sausage on top of the vegetables.
Cover and cook on low until the peppers are soft and the sausage reaches 165°F, about 4 hours (or 2 to 2 1/2 hours on high).
Rest 3 minutes, then slice the sausage and serve with the peppers on rolls or over rice.
